'''Robert Covington''' (born December 14, 1990) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee State Tigers men's basketball|Tennessee State Tigers]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Q&A With Robert Covington|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/qa-robert-covington|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> and, in 2018, he was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]].

==High school career==
Covington attended [[Proviso West High School]] in [[Hillside, Illinois]]. As a senior in 2008–09, he averaged 18 points, 11 rebounds and seven blocks per game, and he was named the West Suburban Conference Player of the Year after leading Proviso West to the West Suburban Championship. He was also an All-Area and All-Conference first-team honoree.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url=http://www.tsutigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19600&ATCLID=204999562 | title=Robert Covington Bio | work=tsutigers.com | access-date=November 12, 2014 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112165941/http://www.tsutigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19600&ATCLID=204999562 | archive-date=November 12, 2014 | df=mdy-all }}</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Tennessee State Tigers men's basketball|Tennessee State]], Covington was named to the [[Ohio Valley Conference]] All-Newcomer team and earned Mid-Major Freshman All-America honors from ''Collegeinsider.com''. In 32 games (28 starts), he averaged 11.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 1.1 steals and 1.1 blocks in 27.3 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/robert-covington-1.html| title=Robert Covington Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | access-date=November 12, 2014}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, Covington recorded eight double-doubles and was named OVC Player of the Week on December 27, 2010. He led the team in rebounds (7.5 rpg), field goal percentage (.500) and three-point field goal percentage (.460). He also led the OVC with his 46% three-point shooting as he earned second-team All-OVC and second-team NABC Division I All-District 19 honors. In 30 games (all starts), he averaged 13.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 1.2 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.0 blocks in 30.8 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, Covington earned first-team All-OVC and first-team NABC Division I All-District 19 honors and was named the 2011–12 ''CollegeInsider.com'' OVC co-MVP. He also earned OVC All-Tournament team and Continental Tire Las Vegas Invitational All-Tournament team honors. At the season's end, he had 1,358 points and 693 rebounds, ranking for 16th and 13th in school history respectively. In 33 games (32 starts), he averaged 17.8 points, 7.9 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 1.5 steals and 1.4 blocks in 31.2 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, Covington earned second-team All-OVC and second-team NABC Division I All-District 19 honors for the second time in his career despite missing ten games due to injury. In 23 games (22 starts), he averaged 17.0 points, 8.0 rebounds, 1.3 assists, 2.3 steals and 1.7 blocks in 31.0 minutes per game. He finished his career ranked seventh on Tennessee State's all-time list in both scoring and rebounding, with 1,749 points and 876 rebounds.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==

===Houston Rockets (2013–2014)===
[[File:Robert Covington of the Houston Rockets (2013).jpg|thumb|right|200px|Covington with the Rockets in 2013]]
After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], Covington joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On July 15, 2013, he signed a multi-year deal with the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/roster-taking-shape-rockets|title=Roster Taking Shape for the Rockets|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2013|access-date=July 15, 2013}}</ref> He spent the majority of the 2013–14 season in the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]] with the Rockets' affiliate team, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]], appearing in just seven NBA games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/covinro01/gamelog/2014/|title=Robert Covington 2013-14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 28, 2018}}</ref> He participated in the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game in February,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://origin.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html|title=Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html|archive-date=February 7, 2014}}</ref> where scored an NBA D-League All-Star record 33 points, 22 of which came in the game's final six minutes, en route to earning MVP honors in the game. He connected on 12 of his 23 shots, including four-of-eight three-pointers at NBA All-Star festivities in New Orleans.<ref name=roy>{{cite web|url=http://origin.nba.com/dleague/news/rgv_vipers_rockets_robert_covington_nba_dleague_rookie_of_year_20_2014_04_18.html|title=RGV's Robert Covington Wins 2014 NBA D-League Rookie of the Year Award|work=NBA.com|date=April 19, 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140426101507/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/rgv_vipers_rockets_robert_covington_nba_dleague_rookie_of_year_20_2014_04_18.html|archive-date=April 26, 2014}}</ref> In April, he was named the NBA D-League Rookie of the Year.<ref name="roy" /> He played in 42 of the Vipers 50 regular season games, 41 as a starter. He averaged a team-high 23.2 points, good for second best in the NBA D-League, while shooting 44 percent from the field. He also averaged 9.2 rebounds and 2.4 steals per game.<ref name="roy" />

After spending [[2014 NBA Summer League|Summer League]], training camp and preseason with the Rockets, Covington was waived on October 27, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-adrien-clark-covington-richmond-and-smith|title=Rockets Waive Adrien, Clark, Covington, Richmond and Smith|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2014|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref>

Covington was selected 3rd overall by the Grand Rapids Drive in the 2015 D-League Draft. However, he did not play for the team.

===Philadelphia 76ers (2014–2018)===
On November 15, 2014, Covington signed a reported five-year contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141115-covington-signed|title=Sixers Sign Free Agent Robert Covington|work=NBA.com|date=November 15, 2014|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=O'Connor|first=Sean|url=https://www.libertyballers.com/2014/11/12/7202395/sixers-likely-to-sign-former-rocket-robert-covington|title=Sixers Likely to Sign Former Rocket Robert Covington|work=libertyballers.com|date=November 12, 2014|access-date=October 28, 2018}}</ref> He made his debut for the 76ers two days later, recording six points, three rebounds, two assists and two steals in {{frac|16|1|2}} minutes off the bench in a 100–75 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141117/PHISAS/gameinfo.html|title=Bonner scores 18, Spurs beat 76ers 100-75|work=NBA.com|date=November 17, 2014|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> On December 3, he scored a career-best 17 points in an 85–77 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Two nights later against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], he set a new career high.<ref name=br1415>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/covinro01/gamelog/2015/|title=Robert Covington 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 28, 2018}}</ref> In 28 minutes, he scored 21 points on 8-of-13 shooting and 3-of-6 from beyond the arc. A day later, he did it again, dropping 25 points on 9-of-14 shooting in 29 minutes off the bench in a 108–101 overtime victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rappaport|first=Max|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141206-covington|title=Big Opportunity, Big Shots From Robert Covington|work=NBA.com|date=December 7, 2014|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> On March 25, he had a second 25-point effort against the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref name="br1415" /> On April 8, Covington scored a career-high 27 points on 8-for-11 shooting in a 119–90 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150408/WASPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Bradley Beal scores 21 points, Wizards beat 76ers|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2015|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> Five days later, he had a third 25-point effort against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref name="br1415" />

After battling injury early in the 2015–16 season, Covington quickly began to excel, leading the NBA with 3.6 steals per game come December.<ref name=steals>{{cite web|url=http://www.tsutigers.com/mbasketball/news/2015-16/6373/robert-covington-excelling-in-second-season-with-nbas-philadelphia-76ers/|title=Robert Covington Excelling in Second Season with NBA's Philadelphia 76ers|work=tsutigers.com|date=December 1, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2018}}</ref> In the final three games of November, Covington secured six-plus steals in each contest, making him the first NBA player to accomplish the feat in three-consecutive games since [[Alvin Robertson]] in 1986.<ref name="steals" /> On November 27, he recorded career highs of 28 points and eight steals in a 116–114 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/game-recap-rockets-116-76ers-114|title=Game Recap: Rockets 116, 76ers 114 - Philadelphia 76ers|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> On December 1, he scored a game-high 23 points to help the 76ers defeat the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] 103–91 and end a 28-game losing streak that began on March 27, 2015, during the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151201/LALPHI/gameinfo.html|title=76ers top Lakers for 1st win of season, snap 28-game skid|work=NBA.com|date=December 1, 2015|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> On February 10, he scored a career-high 29 points and hit a career-high seven three-pointers in a loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160210/SACPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Kings vs 76ers|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> He set a new career high for scoring on April 8 with 30 points against the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160408/NYKPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Knicks vs 76ers|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> On April 12, in a loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]], Covington had his seventh game of the season with six or more three-pointers, joining [[Stephen Curry]], [[Klay Thompson]] and [[J. R. Smith]] as the only players to do so in 2015–16.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160412/PHITOR/gameinfo.html|title=76ers vs Raptors|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> In the team's season finale the following day, Covington scored 27 points and again hit six three-pointers in a 115–105 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/PHICHI/gameinfo.html|title=76ers vs Bulls|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref>

[[File:Bradley Beal, Robert Covington.jpg|thumb|right|246px|Covington drives against [[Bradley Beal]] in 2018]]
On December 14, 2016, Covington had season highs of 26 points and 12 rebounds in a 123–114 loss to the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899816|title=Raptors roll past 76ers 123-114 for 4th straight victory|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2016|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref> On January 20, 2017, he scored 22 points and made two three-pointers in the final 40 seconds to lead the 76ers to a come-from-behind 93–92 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900062|title=Covington, Sixers rally for 93-92 win over Blazers|work=ESPN.com|date=January 20, 2017|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> On January 29, 2017, he scored 21 points and tied his season high of 12 rebounds in a 121–108 loss to the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900137|title=Butler, Lopez lead Bulls to 121-108 win over 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=January 29, 2017|access-date=January 30, 2017}}</ref> In March 2017, he had 13 rebounds on three occasions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/covinro01/gamelog/2017/|title=Robert Covington 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 28, 2018}}</ref> On March 31, he was ruled out for the rest of the season with right knee soreness and swelling.<ref>{{cite web|last=Withers|first=Tom|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/03/31/sixers-shutting-down-jahlil-okafor-and-robert-covington|title=Philadelphia 76ers shutting down Jahlil Okafor, Robert Covington|work=NBA.com|date=March 31, 2017|access-date=March 31, 2017}}</ref>

In the 76ers' season opener on October 18, 2017, Covington scored 29 points in a 120–115 loss to the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974439|title=John Wall scores 28 points, Wizards hold on to beat 76ers|work=ESPN.com|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}}</ref> On November 13, he scored a season-high 31 points against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/covinro01/gamelog/2018/|title=Robert Covington 2017-18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=October 28, 2018}}</ref> On November 17, after restructuring the terms of his contract for the 2017–18 season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/76ers-extend-contract-robert-covington/|title=76ers Extend Contract Of Robert Covington|work=NBA.com|date=November 17, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2017}}</ref> he signed a four-year, $62 million contract extension with the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21427056/philadelphia-76ers-forward-robert-covington-finalizing-four-year-62-million-contract-extension|title=Sources: 76ers, Robert Covington finalizing four-year, $62 million contract extension|work=ESPN.com|date=November 15, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2017}}</ref> In May 2018, he was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/05/23/all-defensive-teams-official-release-2017-18-season|title=Rudy Gobert, Anthony Davis headline 2017-18 NBA All-Defensive first team|work=NBA.com|date=May 23, 2018|access-date=October 28, 2018}}</ref>

Covington started the first 13 games for the 76ers to begin the [[2018–19 Philadelphia 76ers season|2018–19 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/covinro01/gamelog/2019/|title=Robert Covington 2018-19 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 20, 2019}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2018–2020)===
On November 12, 2018, Covington was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], along with [[Jerryd Bayless]], [[Dario Šarić]] and a 2022 second-round pick, in exchange for [[Jimmy Butler]] and [[Justin Patton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-robert-covington-dario-saric-jerryd-bayless-and-future-second|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Robert Covington, Dario Šarić, Jerryd Bayless And A Future Second-Round Draft Pick From Philadelphia|work=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2018|access-date=November 12, 2018}}</ref> He made his debut for the Timberwolves two days later, recording 13 points and seven rebounds in a 107–100 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070889|title=Towns, Wiggins shine as Timberwolves top Pelicans 107-100|work=ESPN.com|date=November 14, 2018|access-date=November 14, 2018}}</ref> On December 31, late in the Timberwolves' loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], Covington sustained a bone bruise on his right knee.<ref>{{cite web|last=Frederick|first=Jace|url=https://www.twincities.com/2019/01/04/timberwolves-robert-covington-will-be-out-a-while-with-bone-bruise-on-his-knee/|title=Timberwolves' Robert Covington will be out 'a while'|work=twincities.com|date=January 4, 2019|access-date=February 27, 2019}}</ref> After missing 23 games,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071585|title=Young, Collins power Hawks past Timberwolves, 131-123 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=February 27, 2019|access-date=February 27, 2019|quote=He has missed 23 consecutive games since suffering the injury on Dec. 31.}}</ref> he was assigned to the [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[NBA G League]] on February 27.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-assign-robert-covington-g-league-affiliate-iowa-wolves|title=TIMBERWOLVES ASSIGN ROBERT COVINGTON TO G LEAGUE AFFILIATE IOWA WOLVES|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2019|access-date=February 27, 2019}}</ref> On March 21, after suffering a setback in his quest for a return, Covington was ruled out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-medical-updates|title=MINNESOTA TIMBERWOLVES MEDICAL UPDATES|work=NBA.com|date=March 21, 2019|access-date=March 21, 2019}}</ref> He underwent successful arthroscopic surgery on April 1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/robert-covington-injury-update|title=ROBERT COVINGTON INJURY UPDATE|work=NBA.com|date=April 1, 2019|access-date=April 2, 2019}}</ref>

===Return to Houston (2020)===
On February 5, 2020, Covington returned to the Rockets in a four-team, 12-player trade with [[Jordan Bell]] from the Timberwolves; Minnesota received [[Jarred Vanderbilt]], [[Malik Beasley]], [[Juan Hernangómez]], [[Evan Turner]], and a 2020 first-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Rockets Complete Four-Team Trade|date=February 6, 2020|publisher=Houston Rockets|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-four-team-trade|access-date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> The following day, Covington made his debut in a 121–111 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], scoring 14 points along with eight rebounds in 30 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Covington has clutch debut, Rockets outlast Lakers 121-111 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161410 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 18, 2020 |date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> On February 29, in a 111–110 overtime win over the [[Boston Celtics]], Covington had 16 points, 16 rebounds, and 3 blocks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Westbrook scores 41, Rockets beat Celtics 111-110 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161534 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=April 18, 2020 |date=February 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2020–2022)===
On November 22, 2020, Covington was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Trevor Ariza]], the draft rights to [[Isaiah Stewart]] and a conditional future first-round pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2020/11/22/blazers-acquire-robert-covington|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE ROBERT COVINGTON FROM HOUSTON|work=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2020}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2022–2023)===
On February 4, 2022, Covington was traded, alongside [[Norman Powell]], to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Eric Bledsoe]], [[Keon Johnson (basketball, born 2002)|Keon Johnson]], [[Justise Winslow]], and a 2025 second-round pick.<ref name="dewald2022">{{cite web | last = Dewald | first = Steve | url = https://www.blazersedge.com/2022/2/4/22918314/trail-blazers-trade-news-latest-nba-rookies-keon-johnson-profile-strengths-weaknesses-grades | date = 4 February 2022 | website = Blazer's Edge | title = Incoming Rookie Brings Defense, Athleticism to Blazers | access-date = 5 February 2022}}</ref><ref name="nba2022a">{{cite web | url = https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-eric-bledsoe-keon-johnson-and-justise-winslow | website = NBA | date = 4 February 2022 | title = Trail Blazers Acquire Eric Bledsoe, Keon Johnson and Justise Winslow | access-date = 5 February 2022}}</ref><ref name="ray2022">{{cite web | title = Former Vol Keon Johnson Traded During First NBA Season | url = https://www.si.com/college/tennessee/football/former-vol-keon-johnson-traded-during-first-nba-season | first = Matt | last = Ray | date=4 February 2022 | access-date=5 February 2022 | website = Fan Nation - Volunteer Country}}</ref> On April 1, Covington logged a career-high 43 points, along with eight rebounds and three blocks, in a 153–119 blowout win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He also made 11 three-pointers during the game, setting a Clippers franchise record for most three-pointers made in a game.<ref name="boxscore1April22">{{cite web | title = Covington, Clippers shred Bucks for 153 as stars sit | url = https://www.nba.com/game/lac-vs-mil-0022101156/box-score | date = 1 April 2022 | website = NBA}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | website = ESPN | date = 1 April 2022 | title = Clippers rip Bucks 153-119 as both teams rest top players | url = https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401360975}}</ref> On May 8, Covington signed a two-year, $24 million extension with the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web |title=LA Clippers Agree To Extension With Robert Covington |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-agree-extension-robert-covington |website=NBA.com |access-date=May 9, 2022 |date=May 8, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=LA Clippers' Robert Covington agrees to 2-year, $24 million extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33862628/la-clippers-robert-covington-agrees-2-year-24-million-extension |access-date=April 8, 2022 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

===Return to Philadelphia (2023–2024)===
On November 1, 2023, the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] acquired Covington, [[Marcus Morris Sr.]], [[Kenyon Martin Jr.]] and [[Nicolas Batum]] from the Clippers in exchange for [[James Harden]], [[P. J. Tucker]], and [[Filip Petrušev]]. As part of the trade, the Clippers dealt a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a pick swap, and cash considerations to the 76ers, while sending a pick swap and cash considerations to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Three-Team Deal with LA Clippers, Oklahoma City Thunder Completed|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-trade-harden-tucker-to-clippers|website=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2023|access-date=November 1, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Covington is the son of Dennis and Teresa Bryant.<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.themonitor.com/sports/rio_grande_valley_vipers/rockets-rookie-forward-covington-grows-up-with-vipers/article_c419cdfc-c061-11e3-8e65-0017a43b2370.html|title=Rockets rookie forward Covington grows up with Vipers|author1=Dennis Silva II |work=TheMonitor.com|access-date=January 20, 2017}}</ref> Covington was in a relationship with [[Germany|German]] model and influencer Amirah Dyme, and on 8 March 2022, she gave birth to their first child together, a daughter named Harmony Faye.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tanizzle - Boy Or Girl? the Gorgeous Cake Queen Amirah Dyme Is Pregnant With Her First Child |url=https://tanizzle.com/articles/260/ |access-date=2022-05-01 |website=Tanizzle |language=en}}</ref> In 2025, he became a brother of [[Alpha Phi Alpha]] fraternity.<ref>{{Cite web |last=watchtheyard |date=2025-04-03 |title=NBA Player Robert Covington Crosses Alpha Phi Alpha |url=https://www.watchtheyard.com/alphas/nba-player-robert-covington-crosses-alpha-phi-alpha/ |access-date=2025-05-16 |website=Watch The Yard |language=en-US}}</ref>
